findings.where: section 4, M8; section 5, P2.3; section 5, phase 3 arms (c) and (d)
findings.claim_in_draft: A harness that sets only what the model reads (the context, the boundary conditions, the question) replaces nothing. And a harness that partitions a task across calls so that no call sees the others' parts deletes the shared constraints between parts
findings.finding: The two sentences sit side by side and say opposite things about the same harness. Arm (d), the partition harness, sets only what the model reads: each call is "handed only the document, the frozen question and the one test". By the first sentence it replaces nothing; by the second it deletes shared constraints. Arm (c) is the same shape (a fixed program writes the context). P2.3 then makes exactly this outcome the falsifier of M8: "If it sets only inputs and still shows the loss, M8 is falsified as written." So P3.2 and P3.3 holding as predicted would falsify M8 by the draft's own criterion. The only escape is that "components" and "shared constraints" mean the language model's ports in one clause and the explanation's parts in the other - an equivocation across two organizations inside one argument, which is what the (F2) sentence the draft quotes is there to forbid.
findings.evidence: Draft: "A harness that sets only what the model reads (the context, the boundary conditions, the question) replaces nothing. And a harness that partitions a task across calls so that no call sees the others' parts deletes the shared constraints between parts: the whole-explanation results (pairs that pull, the best rival, the same-explanation verdict) fall while the part-by-part marks stand." Draft, arm (d): "fresh calls, one per test of Step 5, each handed only the document, the frozen question and the one test". Draft, P2.3: "If it sets only inputs and still shows the loss, M8 is falsified as written." File 10, Part V, quoted by M8: "(F2) prevents a set of locally correct pieces from hiding a lost shared constraint."
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I looked in M8 and in section 7 for a sentence saying which organization each clause is about - the model's components (ports: what to attend to, what to emit next) or the account's parts - and for wording putting arms (c) and (d) outside "a harness that sets only what the model reads". Section 5 calls (d) "the partition harness" and gives it no ports of the model to set. I found no separating sentence.
findings.forced_edit: M8 must name the organization for each clause: the input/output line is about the language model's own components, the partition claim about the parts of the explanation carried across calls. P2.3's criterion must be restricted to the first, or it fires on arms (c) and (d).

findings.claim_in_draft: Phase 5 (the workflow). Its predictions are written in its own plan after phase 4. This file commits only to the form
findings.finding: The draft explains why this order reaches the end goal, and the goal is reached in phase 5. Phase 5 is the one phase with no prediction in this file that could fail, and section 8 ("What follows either way") has no bullet for it at all. Section 9 applies the cannot-fail test to phase 3 only. So the joint that delivers the end goal - phase 4's map to phase 5's workflow - carries no falsifier and no what-follows anywhere in the file; the explanation of the order is unheld exactly where it matters most.
findings.evidence: Draft section 5: "**Phase 5 (the workflow).** Its predictions are written in its own plan after phase 4. This file commits only to the form: the first run is on the reserve (an answer-keyed test, the first in this repository), and the result is a hit and false-alarm count per test of the skill, never a total." Draft section 9: "No prediction of section 5 that phase 3 could falsify surviving the judges: then this is 'a plan that cannot fail' (Planning file 2), and it is not frozen." Section 8's last bullet is "P4.1 or P4.2 fail"; there is no phase 5 bullet.
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I searched sections 5, 8 and 9 for any prediction, count or what-follows naming phase 5 or the workflow, and for any statement that the map's contents are what the workflow needs. The only phase-5 sentences are the form commitment above and section 3's table row "An authority file and a first run on the reserve".
findings.forced_edit: Fix in this file one falsifiable form for phase 5 (for example: at least one "no home" row of section 6 is filled by the workflow's arrangement, and the reserve run reports hit and false-alarm counts per test), or say plainly in section 11 that the phase that reaches the goal carries no falsifier here.

findings.claim_in_draft: P3.4 (from M6). In zero runs does a reader name a rival or a pulling pair whose target was not in its context and not in any file its tool audit shows it read. One falsifies M6 as written.
findings.finding: This cannot fail as worded, on either reading of "target". Read as file 10 reads it - "t, or the organization it targets" - the target of a rival account of document X is X's explanation, and every arm (a) to (d) is handed the document and the frozen question, so the target is in context in every run and the count is zero by construction. Read as the rival's own content, that content is built at the call and so was never in context, and the count is violated in every run. A prediction any outcome satisfies is a label, and M6 - the model's whole answer to Q3 - is left with no run that bears on it.
findings.evidence: Draft M6, quoting file 10 Part IV: "a constructed transport needs an episode 'in which \(t\), or the organization it targets, is available as a represented target'". File 10 line 212: "There is an episode (Part X) whose construction witness prepares \(t\), and in which \(t\), or the organization it targets, is available as a represented target." Draft, arms: "(d) the partition harness: fresh calls, one per test of Step 5, each handed only the document, the frozen question and the one test"; "Same skill (file 33), same documents, same framing."
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I looked for an arm in which a reader is NOT handed the document or the frozen question (which would make the target absent and the count able to move), and for a definition of "target" in section 7's outcome definitions. Section 7 defines a row, a mark, a field's agreement, a phase-2 contradiction and the owner's word, and does not define "target".
findings.forced_edit: Define "target" in section 7 and re-word P3.4 as a count that can move - e.g. an arm in which the document's own explanation is withheld and only a summary of the question given, so that a rival named with no carrier for its target can be seen.

findings.where: section 5, P3.1, P3.2, P3.3; section 7, row "A field agrees between two runs"
findings.claim_in_draft: Arm (c) shows fewer same-explanation verdicts, fewer pulling pairs and fewer rivals than arm (a) ... and its part-by-part marks agree with arm (a) as arm (a) agrees with itself

findings.evidence: H64 Results, "What follows": "Three fields are struck from further use as marked: shape's PART boundary (a written rule is needed), \"turned own test\" (the criterion is reworded or dropped), the same-explanation verdict as a count (kept as quotes only)." H64: "The 'same explanation at this level' verdict on the repeat set: 38 of 48, every disagreement the second marker reading 'nothing tells them apart' as the verdict." Planning file 2, readers-and-markers.md: "Agreement is read by field: the fields that agree carry the claims; the fields that do not are struck as marked and their criteria reworded; disagreements are listed with both markers' words; a third reading settles them, and until it has run nothing is settled." H64 set 1 table: "Tests, RAN versus not | 446 of 528 (84%) | per test: flip 46, pull 45, rival 44 ..."

Section 7 gives only "the same count of verdicts, pairs, rivals", which is a criterion for agreement between two runs, not for what counts as a verdict. Nothing in the draft names H64's strike.
findings.forced_edit: Either reword the same-explanation criterion in section 7 (and say that is a new claim), or drop it as a count and recast P3.2 and P3.3 on pull and rival as RAN-or-not, the only form the record has marked.

findings.claim_in_draft: on more documents than not
findings.finding: A bare majority of documents is a rate used as a pass mark, on an n the phase plan has not yet fixed and that the draft itself calls small. The frozen planning skill forbids exactly this. With three repeats per box and a handful of documents, noise alone clears a bare majority about half the time, so "more documents than not" is a threshold a fault firing one time in ten would also pass.
findings.evidence: Planning file 2, SKILL.md step 6: "Counts first, and a rate only beside its count, never on a small n and never as a pass mark". Planning file 2, "What to watch for": "Three per box is a repeat, better than one and still small: '0 of 6' is compatible with a fault that fires one time in ten." Draft section 10: "**Three per box is small** (Planning file 2: \"0 of 6 is compatible with a fault that fires one time in ten\"). Phase 3's counts are read as counts."
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I looked for a stated number of documents in the draft (there is none: "out of the phase plan's count"), and for any sentence putting a floor under the majority or reading it beside its count rather than as a threshold. Section 5's preamble says only that "the falsifier's shape is fixed here".
findings.forced_edit: Replace "on more documents than not" with a count fixed here against a stated n ("on at least k of n documents, with n at least m"), or state the drop as counts per document, quoted, with no threshold.

findings.claim_in_draft: Falsified if any field's (a)-to-(b) agreement is below the (a)-to-(a) agreement by more than two documents out of the phase plan's count.
findings.finding: A stranger cannot apply this. With three repeats there are three (a)-to-(a) pairs and nine (a)-to-(b) pairs, and the draft fixes no pairing or averaging rule; "two repeats of arm (a)" names no pair. Worse, the yardstick has never been measured: the record holds no within-reader run-to-run field agreement for any skill file, and no reader has ever run under file 33. The record says the variance is large, which would put the baseline so low that (a)-to-(b) could not fall two documents below it - the falsifier could then never fire. Section 9's guard ("with within-arm agreement also low") exists but carries no number, and P3.1 does not invoke it.
findings.evidence: Draft P3.1: "Arms (a) and (b) agree on every field at least as often as two repeats of arm (a) agree with each other." File 54 Results: "Reader variance between runs looks as large as the difference between the two skill modes." H69 Results: "No reader has run under file 32 or 33". Draft section 9: "Phase 3 unable to separate any two arms on any field, with within-arm agreement also low: the marking, not the model, is at fault".
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I searched the record for a recorded run-to-run agreement by field within one reader: H57, H59 and H62 report recurrence counts (0 of 6, 1 of 3) and H64 reports marker-to-marker agreement, not run-to-run field agreement. I found no measured baseline, and no pairing rule in the draft.
findings.forced_edit: P3.1 must say which pairs are compared and how they are combined, and must name the floor on (a)-to-(a) agreement below which the comparison says nothing - the number section 9 leaves blank.

findings.where: section 6, the table and its "would count against"; section 5, P4.1
findings.claim_in_draft: Every operation in the theory's dependence order (section 6's table) is assigned to exactly one holder or to "no home".
findings.finding: Two faults in one line. First, the sketch's own falsifier fires: comparing Part XIV's dependence order with the table, the table has no row for (O), (R), Deploy, (N), (G), (EK) or (U1)-(U3) - not even a "no home" row. Second, the parenthesis "(section 6's table)" makes the table the definition of "the theory's dependence order", so the first clause of P4.1 cannot fail on a left-out operation: the list is whatever the table lists. That is a claim narrowed in advance. Only P4.1's second clause ("At most three operations change holder") is a count that could fail.
findings.evidence: File 10, Part XIV: "(O) and (Q) depend on nothing. (K) depends on (O) and a contract. (F1), (F2), (A) depend on (O), (Q), (K). (E) depends on those. (S), (B), (D) depend on (E). (R) depends on (F1)-(F2) and physical provenance. (K1) depends on (E). Deploy depends on (R) and (CT1). Build depends on histories and (E). (N), (G) depend on Deploy and Build. (P), (EK) depend on (G), (E), Deploy. (RC), (U1)-(U3) depend on all of the above." Section 6's "Where it is" column, in order: "(Q), contract | (E) | (S), (B), (D) | provenance | (K1) | Build | contract, \(H\), index | (P) | receipts, \(h\) | (CT1), (CT2), Can | (RC) | (K), rule signature | \(\mathcal N\)". Draft: "*Would count against the sketch:* ... a judge finding an operation of the dependence order the table leaves out".
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I checked whether the missing items are covered under other names: (F1),(F2),(A) are inside the (E) row and (CT1),(CT2) have their own row, so those are covered. (R) is not the "provenance" row (that row is Part IV's three provenances; M4 treats (R) separately). Deploy, (N), (G), (EK), (U1)-(U3) and (O) appear nowhere in the table, and section 4's "What the model does not claim" excludes them from the MODEL, not from the MAP.
findings.forced_edit: Add rows, or explicit "no home" rows, for (O), (R), Deploy, (N), (G), (EK) and (U1)-(U3); and strike "(section 6's table)" from P4.1 so the clause is tested against Part XIV's list rather than against itself.

findings.where: section 3, "Why the model comes before the skill map"; section 6, first paragraph
findings.claim_in_draft: The theory gives the reason in its own dependence order (Part XIV): what a skill is for is one of the theory's operations (checking an account, finding a question, building, criticising, repairing, keeping receipts), and which of those an agent can carry at one call is exactly what the model says.
findings.finding: Part XIV does not carry this. Its dependence order is an order among the theory's predicates, and the theory has no notion of a skill, a workflow, or an operation a carrier performs: "operation" occurs in file 10 only as "operationalism", "a specified set-theoretic operation" (the query), "a declared restriction operation" and "a licensed operation of the semantics". "A skill is a carrier of one or more of these operations for an agent" is the hinge of the whole map (section 6, Q6, P4.1, P4.2) and of this reason for the order, and it is a construction the theory permits but does not contain - unmarked, against the draft's own rule and against P1.1's "zero unmarked constructions". The reason is also idle for the order: remove the Part XIV sentence and the order does not move, because the dependence order says nothing about which document is written first.
findings.evidence: File 10, Part XIV: "Everything else is derived. Roles, from admitted edits (Part II). Kinds, from signatures (K). ... Nothing depends on a predicate meaning 'really explains,' 'is a cause,' or 'is knowledge.'" Grep of file 10 for "skill", "LLM", "language model", "workflow": no hit ("attention policy" once, Part I; "tokens" once, the coin example). Draft section 6: "A skill is a carrier of one or more of these operations for an agent." Draft's own rule: "where the plan builds something the theory permits but does not contain, it says so."
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I searched file 10 for any sentence making the items of the dependence order things a system performs or carries, and for anything skill-shaped. Part I's "Any aspect of a system's practice - a question, a contract, a transport, a method, an attention policy - can become a target" permits a method as an aspect of practice, so the construction is permitted; I found nothing that contains it.
findings.forced_edit: Mark "a skill is a carrier of the theory's operations" as a construction, with Part I's "a method" as the passage that permits it; and either drop the Part XIV clause from section 3's reason or replace it with the one dependence that does bear on the order (Deploy depends on (R) and (CT1), so retention - M5's territory - precedes any Deploy or Build claim in the map).

findings.claim_in_draft: What an agent instantiates is never read off its emission; it is read off what changes.
findings.finding: Wider than Derivation 9 writes it. The theorem is conditional on two systems sharing an input-output projection: where the projections differ, the projection does distinguish them. The draft's own phase 3 is built on differences between emissions under changed inputs - a function of the projection over a wider input set - so the "never" undercuts the design it is meant to justify. Section 3 states the correct version; M3's headline and section 13's trap do not.
findings.evidence: File 10, Derivation 9: "If \(M_0,M_1\) have the same input-output projection and differ on an account claim, no function of the projection agrees with the claim on both. *Proof.* Equal inputs to a function give equal outputs." Draft section 3, correctly: "Nothing about what an agent instantiates is read off one report; it is read off what changes between reports under admitted changes." Draft section 13: "Reading a reader's report as what the reader instantiates. Derivation 9 forbids it; only what changes between arms is evidence."
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I read Derivation 9 and Part IV's "contents are not identified by having the same outputs" for a sentence dropping the shared-projection condition. Part IV's sentence is about identity of contents, not about what can be read off an emission, and it too is silent on differing projections. I found no unconditional form.
findings.forced_edit: M3's headline and section 13's trap must read "not read off an emission at a fixed input" (or "off an emission a differing model would also produce"), matching section 3's own wording.

findings.claim_in_draft: And Part X's construction needs "an actual subhistory owned by \(s\)" in which the target is "available as a represented target".
findings.finding: The second quotation is not Part X's; it is Part IV's, in the definition of a constructed transport, and it occurs nowhere else in file 10. M6 cites the same words correctly to Part IV, so the draft contradicts itself about where its own quotation comes from. The Status file's claim that "Every quotation of file 10 checked by program" would not catch this: a program checks that a string is present, not that it sits where the sentence says.
findings.evidence: Grep of file 10 for "available as a represented target": one hit, line 212, Part IV: "**Constructed.** There is an episode (Part X) whose construction witness prepares \(t\), and in which \(t\), or the organization it targets, is available as a represented target." File 10, Part X, Build: "holds when an actual subhistory owned by \(s\) and delimited at \(e\) prepares a represented organization for explanatory use of \(c\), contains a nontrivial binding construction relevant to that use, and is not a composition of content-preserving transfers." Draft M6: "Part IV: a constructed transport needs an episode 'in which \(t\), or the organization it targets, is available as a represented target'". Workflow - Status.md: "Every quotation of file 10 checked by program."
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I grepped the whole of file 10 for the phrase and found exactly one occurrence, in Part IV. Part X's Build clause has no such phrase.
findings.forced_edit: Split the citation in M5: "an actual subhistory owned by \(s\)" to Part X, "available as a represented target" to Part IV; and add to the program check that a quotation's Part is checked, not only its presence.

findings.claim_in_draft: a fresh call handed the whole transcript instantiates, at the grain of text, what the stateful agent instantiates, and the two will not differ on any field
findings.finding: The passage M5 quotes bears against this clause rather than holding it. Owned capability requires an owned retained realization "under the same continuity and resource contract", and adds that a description of a protocol is not possession of it. A fresh call handed a transcript has no owned retention and a different continuity - exactly the distinction the quoted sentence draws. M5's headline ("the difference tracks what is represented at each call, not the label") is the draft's own move, not the theory's. The clause is not held by its quoted holder; it is held only by P3.1, a prediction that has not run and whose falsifier I have marked unable to bite.
findings.evidence: File 10, Part XII, quoted by M5: "**Owned capability.** \(\operatorname{Can}_{\Omega,\beta}(\xi,T;\chi)\) requires an owned retained realization or an owned, physically admitted, finite construction of one under the same continuity and resource contract. A theorist's description of a protocol is not the system's possession of it." File 10, (CT2): "\(F(C)\) = states whose executions all complete and return into \(C\)" - which says nothing about carrying "the represented targets of its unfinished work", the content M5 adds to it.
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I searched Parts XII, X and IV for any sentence saying ownership is exhausted by what is represented at a call, or that a carrier handed in at a call is owned. Part IV's (R) makes representation a fidelity fact about the occurrence, the nearest support; it says nothing about ownership or continuity.
findings.forced_edit: M5 must either say its (i) is a construction on CT1/CT2 that the quoted sentence does not contain, or re-word (i) as the weaker claim its holder allows: the two differ on whatever the continuity contract carries and the transcript does not.

findings.claim_in_draft: *Would count against it:* nothing, because it is a frame; it is the one part of the model that is declared, and phase 1 keeps it to this one.
findings.finding: A part the author puts outside the test is not *fixed* - the skill reserves that mark for what the owner put outside the test and said so, and says a designer's free choice is loose. M1 is a free modelling choice with a near neighbour that changes the arms: is "one call" one execution of the serving protocol (one request), one agent turn including its tool calls, or one session? Arm (a), "one Claude Code agent carrying its own history through every step", is one execution under the third reading and many under the first, and M5's (i) and P3.1 depend on which. So M1 is load-bearing and loose, not exempt.
findings.evidence: File 33 reporting.md: "Fixed | The owner put this part outside the test, and said so | that it was not tested. A part that merely serves a fixed job, or that the owner merely asserts (provenance *asserted*), takes whatever mark holds it; a designer's free choice is loose". File 33 SKILL.md: "a free choice is loose". Draft M1: "one call is one execution \(\eta\)". Draft arm (a): "one Claude Code agent (Sonnet 5) carrying its own history through every step of the skill's procedure on a document".
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I looked for an owner's decision putting the grain of a call outside the test: HV Decisions H4, H6, H7, H8 and Semantics S4 say nothing about calls, executions or grain. Section 1 fixes the grain of TEXT, a different index from the grain of a call.
findings.forced_edit: Mark M1 loose, name the neighbour (one request, one turn with its tool calls, one session), and say which reading arms (a) to (d) use - because P3.1 compares an arm that may be one execution with arms that are many.

findings.where: section 5, P1.1, P1.3, P1.4; section 13, second trap
findings.claim_in_draft: The judges, marking the model part by part with the eight marks, leave no part idle and at most two parts loose after their own search for holders. Three or more loose parts and the model is loose as a whole
findings.finding: These predictions make decisions turn on totals of marks and rows, which the frozen skill forbids and which the draft's own trap forbids for the unknowns. P1.4 treats every loose part as worth the same, when the skill's ground is that one part ruling out rivals is worth more than ten that rule out none. The thresholds are also fitted: two loose parts in a ten-part sketch is about the rate the last comparable judging round produced on the planning draft (twelve loose of sixty-six parts). The job P1.4 is really doing - every loose part held or cut before freezing, which its own last clause states - needs no number.
findings.evidence: File 33 SKILL.md: "**No scores.** Do not count confirmations, jobs or parts." and "A table is fine. Never add the marks up." File 33 reporting.md: "**No totals, no ranking by count.** Report by job: what gets done, what fails, and because of which missing part." Draft section 13: "**Counting the six unknowns answered as a score.** One unknown the theory cannot reach matters more than five it can." H69 Results: "**The planning draft, judged the same way**: 66 parts, 38 held, 12 loose, 1 idle, 1 unknown".
findings.what_would_show_wrong: H69 does count marks ("105 held; 13 held if; ... 12 loose; 4 unknown"), which would excuse reporting a count. But its own trap says "Reading '105 of 146 held' as a score. Each holder is quoted in the rig's return; the number is a count of quotes" - it reports counts and refuses to decide on them. P1.1, P1.3 and P1.4 decide on them.
findings.forced_edit: Keep the falsifiers, drop the thresholds: "any part left loose or idle is held or cut before freezing"; "every one of the eleven notions is either given a row or declined with a reason"; "any row that contradicts file 10 is reworded, and the model is rebuilt rather than patched if the contradictions run through its terms rather than its wording."

findings.claim_in_draft: The judges find zero rows that contradict file 10 and zero unmarked constructions.
findings.finding: Both predictions are about what a search returns, not about what is there, and the skill's rule is that found nowhere means unknown. The record shows these searches miss: a blind second marker found breaks in twelve reports the first marker did not, and the word-list scout dropped seven of its own thirty-six findings when made to falsify them - including one it had called absent after searching only where it expected the phrase. So a zero from five judges leaves the rows unknown, not clean.
findings.evidence: File 33 testing-against-cases.md: "**\"Found nowhere\" means unknown.** It shows neither \"unneeded\" nor \"impossible\". \"I did not find X\" describes your search." H64 Results: "**The second marker found breaks in twelve reports the first marker did not**, and they are of a kind the first marker had not looked for". Word-list scout's return, dropped finding: "I had looked only where (F2) is defined and taken absence there for absence everywhere - the exact failure the skill's testing-against-cases warns of".
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I looked for any clause in section 5 or section 7 reading a judge's zero as unknown rather than as clean. Section 7 says "*Held if* and *unknown* follow file 33's readings" for part-marks, but nothing turns P1.1's zero into an unknown.
findings.forced_edit: Word P1.1 and P1.4 as "the judges report zero", and add the reading: a reported zero leaves those rows and parts unknown, with the search described, rather than held.

findings.claim_in_draft: ## 8. What follows either way
findings.finding: Section 8 does not answer every failure it is set against. There is no bullet for P1.3 failing, none for P2.1 finding an unreached part, none for P2.2 being falsified (zero contradictions - its own "the model survives everything and is loose" reading has no consequence anywhere, while P1.4's looseness verdict does), none for P2.3 falsifying M8 before phase 3 runs arm (d) against a part already dead, and none for P3.5. Of section 9's four failure conditions, three answer themselves in a clause and the fourth - a judge showing the programme rests on one of the theory's own attack points as if settled - has no consequence stated anywhere in the file. A failure condition with no consequence cannot bite.
findings.evidence: Draft P2.2: "Zero is read one of two ways, decided by P2.1: if every part was reached, the model survives everything and is loose; if not, the evidence did not reach it. The results file says which." Section 8's bullets, in order: "P1.1 to P1.4 hold", "P1.1 or P1.4 fail", "P1.2 fails", "P2.2 finds contradictions", "P3.1 fails", "P3.2 or P3.3 fail in the direction 'no drop'", "P3.2 or P3.3 fail in the direction 'part-by-part marks drop too'", "P3.4 fails", "P4.1 or P4.2 fail". Section 9, fourth condition: "A judge showing that the programme's use of file 10 rests on one of the theory's own attack points (Part 0, A to E) as if it were settled. The model must not assume sufficiency (A) or that any agent belongs to a class (Part 0's \"does not prove\")."
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I read each of the fourteen predictions of section 5 and each of the four conditions of section 9 against the nine bullets of section 8, and looked in sections 10 to 13 for the missing consequences. Sections 11 and 13 carry prohibitions, not what-follows.
findings.forced_edit: Add bullets for P1.3, P2.1, P2.2-zero, P2.3 and P3.5, and give section 9's fourth condition a consequence (which part is struck, and whether the phase stops).

findings.claim_in_draft: the fields were wrongly sorted into within-step and cross-step; the sorting is redone from the reports, as a new claim, and the run is repeated under the new sorting before anything else follows
findings.finding: This is the one repair route in the plan that re-fits a part to the very reports that broke it, and it does not say the repeat uses fresh documents. Phase 3's documents are held out once; read and marked, they are fitting, so a repeat on the same documents would confirm the new sorting on the cases it was fitted to. The sorting is also the part most exposed to fitting in the first place, because the fields it puts on the "should not drop" side - swap and poke - are two of the four where the record's inter-marker agreement is worst, so the (a)-to-(a) baseline they are compared against is itself the noisiest.

verdict:
## 1. The question, frozen

Taken from the draft's own section 1 and held there. **What is being explained:** why this order of five phases, with these predictions, reaches the owner's end goal - "The end goal is an entire workflow that embodies the yet incomplete semantics theory HV is based on" (HV decision H6, quoted whole in Workflow/ORIGIN.md). **Over what range:** this repository's five projects, the evidence in hand named in section 2, and the runs section 5 says can be made. **What is asked:** *does it achieve its purpose?* - a purpose question about an order of work, answered forward (each phase is claimed to produce what the next needs). Not asked and not tested here: whether the model is true, whether a rival plan is better (another judge's task), anything at the grain of weights.

I did not change this question. Where I ran a finer one I say so: the finer question "would a differently-ordered programme give the same products?" is recorded below, under *look inside*, as new.

## 2. The explanation in parts, and the jobs

**Parts** (the draft's own numbering): the five phases and their order, as four joints 1→2, 2→3, 3→4, 4→5; the three "why" paragraphs of section 3 (W1 model before map, W2 phase 2 a reading, W3 phase 3 the first test); the sketch M1-M10; the fourteen predictions P1.1-P4.2 and the phase 5 form; the skill-map sketch of section 6 with its premise "A skill is a carrier of one or more of these operations for an agent"; the five outcome definitions of section 7; the nine "what follows" bullets of section 8; the four failure conditions of section 9.

**Jobs, tagged.**
*Given* (the owner named it): the end goal, quoted above; Q1 the harness ("difficult to implement without destroying the already latent LLM capabilities"); Q2 "The capabilities seem to be centred around statefull vs stateless agents"; Q3 "built in context should consume part of the reasoning architecture specified in the semantics"; Q4 "Externalising parts of memory are still important, and relevant to managing attention"; Q5 "Whether LLMs guide attention in planning, exploration and execution is yet unknown"; Q6 "Which skills to have, and where the boundaries lie is the first step. Right now we have planning and HV."
*Fixed* (the owner put it outside the test and said so): HV file 33 and Planning file 2 frozen (H6, "Harden HV and planning right now, freeze them"); the other projects read only (H8, "Do not ever edit or touch other projects. This is read only."); who may run (H4, "Never test on Fable 5.1 subagents"; H7, "Use Opus 5 as subagents ... effort levels to Extra, not max", with the owner's correction "There is no need for 20 different agents. 5 tops" recorded in H69); file 10 and only file 10 (S4, "No no. 20 was a regression. Hence I never supplied it"); every phase on the owner's word (Planning file 2, itself frozen).
*Added* (the draft put it there; each named): that the model reaching phase 3 must have met the evidence in hand; that a map drawn before the model would be drawn by habit; that at most three operations may change holder; that no part may be idle and at most two loose; that at least six of eleven notions get a row; that five of six unknowns get a runnable falsifier; that fields sort into within-step and cross-step; that a skill is a carrier of the theory's operations; that phase 5 runs the first answer-keyed test.

A part held only by an added job is *held if*, and section 3 says so.

## 3. Part by part
